subject: physics_2
question_text: Derive an expression for the potential at a distance from a point charge.

verification.note: The 1+2+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: F = qq₀/4πε₀x², dW = −F dx with the sign carried by force opposing the inward movement; ∫x⁻²dx = −1/x gives W = qq₀/4πε₀ (1/r − 0) = qq₀/4πε₀r; V = W/q₀ = q/4πε₀r — matches the book's chain, with the book's ω for work written as W.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Setup and definition
lines: A positive point charge q is at O. P is a
point at a distance r from O. The potential
at P is the work done in bringing a unit
positive test charge from infinity to P.
A test charge q₀ is brought in against the
field of q. At a distance x from O the field
steps.margin_note: First mark. The definition of potential — work per unit test charge from infinity — must be written.
steps.why: The whole derivation is this definition turned into an integral: potential is defined through work, so the work from infinity to P is what must be computed.
common_mistakes: Starting the integral without defining V as work per unit charge from infinity.
Writing the field with 1/x instead of 1/x². The FIELD falls as 1/x²; the POTENTIAL falls as 1/x.

recall.must_convey: That potential at P is the work done per unit test charge in bringing it from infinity, and the field at distance x is q by 4 pi epsilon-nought x squared.
accept: work per unit charge from infinity
test charge brought from infinity to P
field q by four pi epsilon nought x squared
reject: V equals q by four pi epsilon nought r

steps.memory_tip: Definition first: potential is work per unit charge, carried in from infinity.

steps.label: The figure
steps.margin_note: The line from O through P, with the small step dx between B and A far out on the line.
steps.why: The picture fixes the direction bookkeeping: the test charge moves from A to B, toward O, while the force of q on it points away from O — which is where the minus sign in dW = −F dx comes from.
common_mistakes: Placing dx near O instead of out along the line — dx is a step of the JOURNEY from infinity.

recall.must_convey: That a line is drawn from the charge at O through P, with a small step dx between points B and A.
accept: draw O P and the line
small step dx between B and A

steps.memory_tip: One line, four letters O P B A, one small step dx.

steps.label: The work integral
lines: The force on q₀ at a distance x from O is
Moving q₀ from A to B through dx toward O,
the force and the displacement are opposite,
so the work done on the charge is
Adding every step from infinity to P:

lines.text: W = −∫ (qq₀ / 4πε₀x²) dx, x from ∞ to r

steps.margin_note: Two marks. The minus sign, the limits ∞ to r, and the integration are the working.
steps.why: The force changes with x, so work must be integrated, not multiplied. Integrating 1/x² gives −1/x; with the minus sign of dW and the limits ∞ to r, the two minus signs cancel and W comes out positive — as it must, since pushing q₀ toward q takes work.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign in dW = −F dx, which makes W come out negative.
Writing the limits r to ∞ instead of ∞ to r. The journey STARTS at infinity.
Multiplying F by r instead of integrating — F is not constant.

recall.must_convey: That dW = minus F dx is integrated from infinity to r, giving W = qq₀ by 4 pi epsilon-nought r.
accept: integrate minus F dx from infinity to r
q q nought by four pi epsilon nought r
reject: V equals W by q nought

steps.memory_tip: One power of x is spent in the integration: a 1/x² force leaves a 1/x work.

steps.label: The potential
lines: The potential at P is this work per unit
V is a scalar and falls as 1/r, not 1/r².
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Divide by q₀ and box V = q/4πε₀r.
steps.why: Dividing by q₀ removes the test charge from the answer — the potential belongs to the point P and the source q alone, which is why every test charge measures the same V.
common_mistakes: Leaving q₀ in the final answer. The potential must not depend on the test charge.
Writing r² in the denominator — that is the field, not the potential.

recall.must_convey: That V equals W by q-nought, giving q by 4 pi epsilon-nought r.
accept: V is W by q nought
q by four pi epsilon nought r
potential falls as one by r
heard_as: V equals W by q nought

steps.memory_tip: Field 1/r², potential 1/r — the integral costs one power of r.

insider_note: The two working marks live in the integral: the minus sign of dW = −F dx and the limits ∞ to r are what the examiner checks first.
